- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ levels), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the magnitude of the drop.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds too much upward bias after peaks, ignoring the tendency to revert to lower levels.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing downward trends — often misses the start of a decline until 5–7 days later.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then become overly pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggesting a “U-shaped” bias.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonality or calendar effects — e.g., consistent underperformance in late January/early February.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility — forecasts spike after a single high or low, then fail to correct.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market shocks — e.g., sudden drops after regulatory announcements are not captured early enough.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp drops and overestimates gradual declines.
- Model often fails to recognize the “tail risk” — underestimates the probability of extreme downward moves after a peak.
